questions.prompt: Complete the intention: "Rania ___ become a biologist."
questions.explanation: An intention uses am / is / are + going to + base verb, and Rania is "she", so: Rania is going to become a biologist. "going to" alone drops the verb "is", which English cannot leave out; "is go to" loses the -ing of "going"; "will going to" mixes two future forms.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expresses a planned action?

options.text: She is going to visit Rome one day.
She is visiting Rome next week.

questions.explanation: A planned action is am / is / are + verb + ing + a future word: she is visiting Rome next week. "is going to visit" + base verb is an intention, not a planned action; "visits … every summer" is a habit in the simple present; "wants to visit" only tells a wish.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct negative: "The car of the future ___ use petrol."
questions.explanation: The negative of the future tense is will not, shortened to won't, + bare infinitive: the car won't use petrol. "doesn't will" adds do to will, which never happens; "willn't" is not an English word; "not will" puts not in the wrong place.

After be thinking of, the verb takes -ing, because "of" is a preposition: I'm thinking of studying abroad. "to study" is the form that follows "intend to", not "thinking of"; "study" and "studied" are not possible after "of".

questions.prompt: Complete: "Kate ___ rent a house with her friends."
questions.explanation: intend is an ordinary verb in the present, so with Kate (she) it takes -s, and it is followed by to + base verb: Kate intends to rent a house. "intend to" forgets the -s; "intends" without "to" drops the "to" before the base verb; "is intend to" adds "is" to a simple present verb.
